subject: Environment
sub_topic: National Green Tribunal — jurisdiction and benches

concepts.name: Establishment and Constitutional/Statutory Basis of NGT
key_dimensions: NGT Act 2010 as the parent legislation — not a constitutional body but a statutory tribunal
Distinction from constitutionally mandated bodies (e.g., NHRC, CEC) — UPSC trap on 'constitutional vs statutory'
Directive Principles (Art. 48A) and Fundamental Right (Art. 21) as philosophical underpinnings
Global comparisons: NGT as one of the few dedicated environment tribunals worldwide (alongside Australia's Land and Environment Court)

concepts.name: Original Jurisdiction of NGT
key_dimensions: Scope: Substantial questions relating to environment including enforcement of legal rights
Who can file: 'Any person' — broad locus standi, not restricted to aggrieved party
Applicability only to the 7 scheduled Acts listed in Schedule I of NGT Act
Trap: NGT cannot take suo motu cognizance (unlike Supreme Court under Art. 32) — critical distinction

concepts.name: Appellate Jurisdiction of NGT
key_dimensions: Appeals against orders/decisions of authorities under the 7 scheduled Acts (e.g., MoEF&CC, SEIAA)
Time limit: Appeal must be filed within 30 days of the impugned order (extendable by 60 more days for sufficient cause)
Trap: Not all environmental orders are appealable to NGT — only those under Schedule I Acts
Distinction between original vs appellate jurisdiction in terms of parties and timelines

concepts.name: The Seven Scheduled Acts (Schedule I) — Scope and Gaps
key_dimensions: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1974; Air Act 1981; Environment Protection Act 1986; Forest Conservation Act 1980; Biological Diversity Act 2002; Public Liability Insurance Act 1991; National Environment Tribunal Act 1995
UPSC trap: Wildlife Protection Act 1972 is NOT in Schedule I — NGT has no direct jurisdiction
Implications of exclusion: Cases involving wildlife, Indian Forest Act 1927, or EIA notifications may fall outside NGT's primary jurisdiction
Debates on expanding Schedule I to include more statutes

concepts.name: Exclusion of Wildlife Protection Act and Its Implications
key_dimensions: WPA 1972 is absent from Schedule I — NGT cannot adjudicate disputes purely under WPA
However, NGT can deal with wildlife matters if they involve EPA 1986 or Forest Conservation Act 1980 linkages
High Court writ jurisdiction remains intact for WPA matters — overlap and forum selection issues
Judicial clarifications: Supreme Court in various cases on where wildlife-forest overlap matters should go

concepts.name: Composition of NGT — Judicial and Expert Members
key_dimensions: Chairperson: Must be a retired Judge of the Supreme Court
Judicial Members: Retired High Court Judges; minimum 10, maximum 20
Expert Members: Must have a doctorate or 15 years' experience in environment/forest/science — minimum 10, maximum 20
UPSC trap: NGT is a multi-disciplinary body — both legal and technical expertise mandatory, unlike ordinary courts

concepts.name: Principal Bench and its Location
key_dimensions: Principal Bench located at New Delhi
Chairperson sits at the Principal Bench
Jurisdiction of Principal Bench extends pan-India for matters not assigned to other benches
Significance: All appeals from Circuit/Zonal Benches in certain matters may be routed through Principal Bench

concepts.name: Zonal Benches of NGT — Locations and Territorial Jurisdiction
key_dimensions: Four Zonal Benches: Bhopal (Central), Pune (Western), Kolkata (Eastern), Chennai (Southern)
Each bench covers specific states — UPSC frequently tests which state falls under which bench
Trap: No bench in the Northeast — northeastern states currently covered by Principal Bench or Kolkata bench
Circuit Benches: NGT can also hold circuit sittings at other locations for convenience

concepts.name: Relief and Compensation Powers of NGT
key_dimensions: NGT can award compensation to victims of pollution/environmental damage and restore damaged environment
'Polluter Pays Principle' codified — NGT can impose costs on violators
No upper monetary cap on compensation — unlike consumer forums
Trap: NGT cannot impose imprisonment — it is a civil tribunal; criminal liability still goes to criminal courts

concepts.name: Penalty for Non-Compliance with NGT Orders
key_dimensions: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine up to Rs. 10 crore, or both for non-compliance
If non-compliance is by a company: fine up to Rs. 25 crore
Trap: The imprisonment provision exists for non-compliance, NOT for the environmental violation itself
NGT can transmit orders to Civil Court for execution — enforcement mechanism

concepts.name: Limitation Period for Filing Applications before NGT
key_dimensions: Original applications: 5 years from the date when cause of action first arose
Appellate applications: 30 days from impugned order (extendable by 60 days)
Trap: Different limitation periods for original vs appellate jurisdiction — common exam confusion
Discretion to condone delay beyond prescribed period for sufficient cause shown

concepts.name: Relationship Between NGT and High Courts — Jurisdictional Overlap
key_dimensions: NGT does not oust High Court's writ jurisdiction under Art. 226 — both can technically entertain environment matters
Supreme Court's stance: Parties should prefer NGT as a specialized forum over High Courts for scheduled Act matters
However, High Courts can entertain cases involving non-Schedule I Acts (e.g., WPA)
UPSC trap: NGT is NOT a substitute for the Supreme Court — appeals from NGT go directly to the Supreme Court, not High Court

concepts.name: Appeal from NGT Orders — Hierarchy
key_dimensions: Appeals from NGT lie directly to the Supreme Court of India (not to any High Court)
Time limit for appeal to Supreme Court: 90 days from the date of NGT order
Trap: This creates a unique appellate hierarchy — bypassing High Courts entirely
Rationale: Prevent multiplicity of proceedings and forum shopping in High Courts

concepts.name: NGT and the 'Precautionary Principle'
key_dimensions: NGT explicitly mandated to apply the precautionary principle in adjudication
Section 20 of NGT Act: NGT shall apply principles of sustainable development, precautionary principle, and polluter pays
Trap: These principles are guiding principles for NGT, not just judicial interpretations — they are statutory obligations
Comparison with courts: Supreme Court evolved these principles through case law (Vellore Citizens case); NGT has them by statute

concepts.name: NGT vs National Environment Appellate Authority (NEAA) — Predecessor Comparison
key_dimensions: NEAA (1997) was the predecessor body — had very limited jurisdiction only over EIA-related approvals
NGT replaced NEAA and National Environment Tribunal (NET) — broader mandate
UPSC trap: NEAA was dissolved upon NGT's establishment; knowing the transition is important
Key improvement: NGT has expert members + broader jurisdiction + compensation powers unlike NEAA

concepts.name: Suo Motu Powers — Absence and its Significance
key_dimensions: NGT cannot take suo motu cognizance — requires a petition/application to invoke jurisdiction
Contrast with Supreme Court (Art. 32) and High Courts (Art. 226) which can act suo motu
Debate: Should NGT be given suo motu powers given environmental urgency? — policy discussion angle
Practical implication: Delays in filing can mean environmental damage is irreversible before NGT can act

concepts.name: Interim Relief Powers of NGT
key_dimensions: NGT can grant interim relief, stay orders, and injunctions pending final disposal
Standard: 'Prima facie case, balance of convenience, irreparable harm' — similar to civil court standards
Trap: NGT's interim orders are binding and enforceable immediately — non-compliance attracts same penalties as final orders
Examples: Stay on construction in eco-sensitive zones, interim closure of polluting industries

concepts.name: Role of NGT in Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Disputes
key_dimensions: EIA notifications issued under EPA 1986 — falls within Schedule I, so NGT has jurisdiction
NGT can examine procedural violations in EIA process (inadequate public hearing, flawed baseline data)
Trap: NGT cannot rewrite or substitute its own EIA — it can only quash and remand to competent authority
Landmark cases: Kudankulam, Navi Mumbai Airport cases challenged before NGT on EIA grounds

concepts.name: NGT's Power to Restore Environment — 'Restitution' Jurisdiction
key_dimensions: Beyond compensation, NGT can order restitution of damaged property and restoration of environment
Can create special funds for environmental restoration managed by a designated authority
Trap: This goes beyond typical tribunal powers — NGT has quasi-executive functions in directing restoration
Distinction: Compensation = monetary relief to victims; Restoration = ecological repair — both can be ordered simultaneously

concepts.name: Quorum and Bench Composition for Hearing Cases
key_dimensions: Each bench must have at least one Judicial Member and one Expert Member — ensures interdisciplinary adjudication
Trap: A bench of only judicial members (without expert member) is not validly constituted for NGT purposes
Chairperson can constitute special benches for urgent or complex matters
Significance of expert member: Can examine technical reports, pollution data, environmental studies directly
